## Warm-up 🔥 {.smaller}

⏱️ 10 min

```r
gc <- c(0.55, 0.41, 0.62, 0.38, 0.71)
```

1. Print the mean
2. Print only values above 0.5
3. How many are above 0.5? (hint: `sum(gc > 0.5)`) 🤔

::: notes
0–10 min. Point 3 is a lovely R trick: TRUE counts as 1.
:::

## Reading real data 📄 {.smaller}

Remember `results/report.txt` from your Python tool? Let's analyse it in R.

```r
seqs <- read.csv("results/report.txt", sep = "\t")

head(seqs)
str(seqs)        # structure: columns and their types 🔍
summary(seqs)    # min, max, mean per column 📊
nrow(seqs)
```

. . .

**Python produced the data. R analyses it.** 🐍🤝🇷

::: notes
10–25 min. This is the payoff: their own pipeline now spans two languages.
Make sure their report has a header row — otherwise read.csv guesses wrong.
:::

## Your first plot 📈

```r
hist(seqs$length,
     main = "Sequence length distribution",
     xlab = "Length (bp)",
     col  = "steelblue")
```

. . .

One line, and you have a figure 🎉

::: notes
The instant plot is R's best first impression. Show it live.
:::

## Three plots you will actually use {.smaller}

```r
hist(seqs$gc)                       # distribution 📊

plot(seqs$length, seqs$gc,          # relationship 🔗
     xlab = "Length", ylab = "GC",
     pch = 19, col = "darkgreen")

boxplot(gc ~ species, data = seqs)  # compare groups 📦
```

. . .

`main` `xlab` `ylab` `col` work almost everywhere.

## Saving a figure 💾

```r
png("results/gc_plot.png", width = 800, height = 600)
hist(seqs$gc, main = "GC content", col = "steelblue")
dev.off()          # ⚠️ don't forget this — it closes the file!
```

. . .

Now your figure is a file you can put in a report or a thesis 📄

::: notes
25–35 min. dev.off() is the classic forgotten line — the file stays empty without it.
:::

## A word on ggplot2 🎨 {.smaller}

```r
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(seqs, aes(x = length, y = gc)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "GC vs length")
```

. . .

Prettier, more powerful, and a whole language of its own.
Base R plots are enough for today — ggplot2 is your next step 🌱

::: notes
Mention only. Going deeper needs a full block; point them to resources instead.
:::

## Exercise: Analyse your own data 🧬 {.smaller}

⏱️ 30 min · breakout rooms · switch after 15 min

Create `scripts/plot_report.R`:

1. Run your Python tool to produce a tab-separated report 🐍
2. Read it into R with `read.csv(..., sep = "\t")`
3. Print `summary()` and the number of rows
4. Make a histogram of lengths 📊
5. Make a scatter plot of length vs GC 🔗
6. Save one figure into `results/` and commit the **script** (not the PNG 🙈)

💡 **Bonus:** colour the points by whether GC is above 50%

::: notes
35–75 min. Most common failure: wrong path or missing header. Have a ready CSV in the chat as plan B.
:::

## Wrap-up ✅ {.smaller}

- `read.csv()` brings data in 📄
- `summary()` and `str()` before anything else 🔍
- `hist()` `plot()` `boxplot()` — one line each 📊
- `png()` … `dev.off()` to save 💾

**Homework** 🏠 Commit your R script.
